chunks: Fadalah narrated from Aban that Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said:

Regarding a child who matures and then chooses Christianity, while one of his parents is a Christian or both are Muslims, he said: He is not to be left alone, but rather he is to be compelled toward Islam.

key_terms.أَبَوَيْهِ: his two parents, whose religious status affects the ruling
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a child or minor under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّةَ: Christianity, the religion chosen in the case described
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion to which he is compelled
key_terms.لَا يُتْرَكُ: he is not to be left as he is
key_terms.مُسْلِمَيْنِ: being two Muslims; describing both parents as Muslim
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ: he is to be struck or compelled as disciplinary enforcement

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a child who reaches maturity and chooses Christianity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a child who reaches maturity and adopts Christianity in a case where parental religious status connects him to Islam. It indicates that such a person is not to be left upon that choice, but is to be forced back to Islam according to the ruling stated here.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3554 - In a narration reported by Fadalah from Aban, Abu Abdullah (as) said:

"Regarding a child who grows up and chooses Christianity while one of his parents is a Christian or both of them are Muslims, he is not to be left (in that state), but rather he is compelled to follow Islam."
